newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-NETS' CALIPARI, HEAT'S HALBERSTAM FINED FOR REMARKS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-NETS' CALIPARI, HEAT'S HALBERSTAM FINED FOR REMARKS.

text.p: NBA commissioner David Stern fined New Jersey Nets coach John Calipari $25,000 and Miami Heat broadcaster David Halberstam $2,500 on Wednesday for recent offensive remarks.

Stern said he felt both Calipari and Halberstam were "fully aware of the offensive nature of their remarks, and I believe they genuinely regret not only making them but also the pain they may have caused others.

"I nonetheless believe that a clear message must be sent that such statements and the sentiments they convey -- whether intended or not -- are unacceptable from individuals associated with the NBA," Stern said in a strong statement that accompanied the announcement of the fines.

Calipari was fined for using an ethnic slur in a profanity-laced arguement with Newark Star-Ledger basketball writer Dan Garcia last Thursday. In the heated exchange with Garcia in a parking lot, Calipari called the reporter a "Mexican idiot."

Reports of the use of the ethnic slur by Calipari sparked numerous columns in other local newspapers calling for his firing. The Nets coach has since apologised publicly and in writing to Garcia, who covers the Nets for the Star-Ledger.
Halberstam's offensive remark came during a radio broadcast of a Heat game last Friday after John Crotty made a particularly outstanding pass.

"Thomas Jefferson would have been proud of that pass from Crotty," Halberstam said. "When Thomas Jefferson was around, basketball was not invented yet, but those slaves working at Thomas Jefferson's farm, I'm sure they would have made good basketball players."
Crotty went to college at Virginia, which was founded by Jefferson.

Stern said: "These gentlemen -- and everyone associated with the NBA -- should understand that racially insensitive or derogatory comments are not acceptable, and perhaps the widespread coverage that the issue has received will serve the purpose of delivering this message to an even broader audience."

The disparity in the fines was not intended to reflect any judgment of which remark was more offensive, Stern said, but resulted from "a realistic acknowledgment of the differing financial impact that fines will have on the individuals involved."
Stern said such disciplinary action by his office had historically been limited to comments about the game and called Wednesday's action "unchartered territory for an NBA commissioner."
